name: John Hughes
milestone_by_age_26: Oxford DPhil awarded around 1984 (age ~25–26) is the main dated early credential, but major field impact arrived later with 'Why Functional Programming Matters' (1989, age ~31), Haskell community leadership, and QuickCheck/QuviQ; no clearly extraordinary dated material breakout by 26 beyond a standard research doctorate.
early_history_summary: Born 15 July 1958; completed a University of Oxford DPhil (thesis on design and implementation of programming languages, mid-1980s). Later joined Chalmers, co-shaped Haskell, co-developed QuickCheck, and cofounded QuviQ.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Chalmers profiles confirm 1958 birth and 1984 Oxford DPhil; influential FP work and QuickCheck came after age 26.

name: Sergio Villarreal
category: Unverified tech candidate (Slack founder label appears incorrect)
milestone_by_age_26: Batch note labels him as 'Slack founder,' but Slack was founded by Stewart Butterfield, Eric Costello, Cal Henderson, and Sergd Serban; no verifiable public biography tying a Sergio Villarreal to Slack founding or another dated material tech milestone by age 26 was found.
early_history_summary: No authoritative public biography matching the curated Slack-founder claim was located; multiple professionals share the name without a clear match to the stated milestone.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia Slack founder list and web search do not support the batch occupation claim; candidate remains unverified for age-26 eligibility.

name: Andrei Alexandrescu
milestone_by_age_26: BS Electrical Engineering from Politehnica Bucharest in 1994 (age ~25) and a student informatics contest success in 1993 are the main dated items by 26; breakout recognition arrived with first C/C++ Users Journal article (1998, age ~29) and Modern C++ Design (2001, age ~32).
early_history_summary: Born 1969 in Bucharest; classical guitar competition prizes in teens; began programming in college; BS 1994; moved to the U.S. in 1998; later UW PhD, Facebook research scientist, D language co-designer, Nvidia principal research scientist.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and personal site confirm 1969 birth, 1994 BS, and post-26 publications/books that made his reputation.

name: Yuri Burda
milestone_by_age_26: No reliable public birth year or dated early-career milestone by age 26 found; known mainly as an OpenAI researcher (e.g., grokking/scaling and GPT-related technical report authorship) without a verifiable age-bounded breakout.
early_history_summary: Public footprint is primarily OpenAI research contributions and coauthorships; biographical dates and pre-OpenAI timeline are not well documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: OpenAI paper authorships establish professional identity but not birth year or age-26 milestone dating.

name: Douglas Engelbart
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26 (1951) he had Navy radar/radio technician service and an Oregon State EE BS (1948, age ~23) plus early NACA/Ames work, but the material HCI breakouts—Augmenting Human Intellect (1962), mouse development, and the 1968 Mother of All Demos—came well after 26.
early_history_summary: Born Portland 1925; rural Oregon childhood after father died; Franklin High School; Navy WWII service where he read Vannevar Bush; BS EE Oregon State 1948; Ames wind-tunnel work; Berkeley MS/PhD mid-1950s; SRI ARC and NLS later defined his legacy.
family_context_summary: Middle of three children; father Carl died when Douglas was about nine; family of German/Swedish/Norwegian descent in Oregon.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as a computing or engineering apprenticeship path.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Engelbart Institute materials place landmark demos and inventions decades after age 26.

name: James C. Browne
milestone_by_age_26: In 1960 at age 24–25 he earned a PhD in physical chemistry/chemical physics from the University of Texas at Austin (thesis on electronic energy of helium hydride) and joined the UT Physics faculty the same year.
early_history_summary: Born Conway, Arkansas, 16 June 1935; father managed a hardware store. Conway High School, BA chemistry Hendrix College 1956, then UT Austin graduate work under Albert Matsen. Faculty career spanned physics and the founding years of UT Computer Science; later Queen’s University Belfast computing lab leadership and decades of parallel systems research.
primary_leverage_engine: Early elite research doctorate and faculty placement
family_context_summary: Born to Walter Everett Browne (hardware store manager) and Louise Catherine James Browne in Conway, Arkansas; middle-class small-city upbringing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father managed a hardware store; not a computing domain apprenticeship, though a stable working/managerial household.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Hendrix College, UT Austin PhD, early faculty appointment, Matsen supervision
evidence_summary: UT Physics history and Wikipedia agree on 1935 birth, 1956 Hendrix BA, 1960 UT PhD, and 1960 physics faculty start at age ~25. Father’s hardware-store occupation is documented; later CS founding faculty role (1968) and Belfast computing center leadership extended the trajectory. Family computing advantage is not documented.
starting_point: Born 1935 in Conway, Arkansas, to a hardware-store manager father and local Arkansas parents; liberal-arts chemistry path at Hendrix then UT Austin graduate school.
current_position: Died 19 January 2018 at age 82 in Austin; final roles included UT Austin Regents Chair #2 in Computer Sciences (emeritus), professor of physics/ECE, and TACC-related CTO work on Ranger.

trajectory.event: Earned BA in chemistry from Hendrix College and began graduate study at UT Austin.
Completed UT Austin PhD in physical chemistry and joined the UT Physics faculty.
Became Professor of Computer Science at Queen’s University Belfast and helped establish its computational center.
Returned to UT as professor of physics and computer science; among first CS department faculty and later department chair.
Received UT Austin Career Research Excellence Award after decades spanning ~500 papers and dozens of PhD students.
Died in Austin after a multi-decade career as a parallel computing and systems research leader.

name: Jan Koum
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26 (2002) he had immigrated to the U.S., self-taught programming, joined w00w00, and was working as a Yahoo infrastructure engineer (hired ~1997, age ~21), but the material breakout—incorporating WhatsApp on his 33rd birthday in 2009 and the later Facebook acquisition—came well after 26.
early_history_summary: Born Kyiv 1976; raised in Fastiv; immigrated with mother/grandmother to Mountain View at 16; worked as grocery cleaner; SJSU dropout; Yahoo ~9 years with Brian Acton; founded WhatsApp 2009.
family_context_summary: Jewish family from Ukraine; father stayed in Ukraine and died 1997; mother worked as babysitter, family on social support in California; mother died 2000 after cancer.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not a tech-domain family apprenticeship; economic hardship after immigration.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Forbes rags-to-riches profiles place WhatsApp founding at age 33; pre-26 work is ordinary early engineering employment.

name: Samuel Buss
milestone_by_age_26: Emory bachelor's 1979 and Princeton master's 1983 (age ~25–26) fall within the window, but the defining results—bounded arithmetic PhD thesis (1985, age ~28) and STOC publication of the Boolean formula value problem in ALOGTIME (1987, age ~29–30)—came after 26.
early_history_summary: Born 6 August 1957; Emory BA 1979; Princeton MS 1983 and PhD 1985 under Simon Kochen; Berkeley lecturer then UCSD professor from 1988; major figure in bounded arithmetic and proof complexity.
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and UCSD profiles date PhD 1985 and STOC 1987 after age 26; master's alone is not treated as the material breakout.

name: Gary Wang
category: FTX CTO and cofounder, crypto engineer
milestone_by_age_26: In or around October 2017 at about age 24, he left Google Flights and co-founded Alameda Research with Sam Bankman-Fried; in 2019 at about age 26 he co-founded crypto exchange FTX as CTO.
early_history_summary: Born ~1993 in China; moved to the U.S. at age 8; Cherry Hill High School East 2011; Canada/USA Mathcamp where he met Bankman-Fried; MIT math/CS, multi-year roommate of SBF; Google Flights engineer on price aggregation; co-founded Alameda (2017) then FTX (2019); later pleaded guilty and cooperated in the FTX fraud cases.
primary_leverage_engine: Scarce systems engineering depth + high-trust cofounder
secondary_engine: Network / capital (SBF peer team; crypto market wave)
family_context_summary: Chinese immigrant parents; family moved to U.S. when he was 8; later Cherry Hill, NJ. Detailed wealth/class not richly documented beyond immigrant professional path.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as a finance/crypto domain apprenticeship in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: MIT, Mathcamp peer SBF, Google Flights systems work, Alameda/FTX cofounder, crypto wave
evidence_summary: Wikipedia, SEC complaint, and major press agree he co-founded Alameda (~2017) and FTX (2019) with Bankman-Fried after MIT and Google Flights, at ages ~24 and ~26. Peak Forbes ranking and later guilty plea/cooperation define the arc. Family finance details remain thin; strongest early advantages are MIT pipeline and the SBF partnership.
starting_point: Born ~1993 in China; immigrated to the U.S. at age 8; raised in New Jersey (Cherry Hill) and trained in math/CS at MIT.
current_position: Former FTX CTO; pleaded guilty to fraud-related charges, cooperated against Bankman-Fried, and received a sentence that avoided prison time after cooperation (2024).

trajectory.event: Graduated Cherry Hill High School East after Mathcamp connection with Sam Bankman-Fried.
Completed MIT math/CS studies and joined Google Flights engineering.
Left Google and co-founded Alameda Research with Bankman-Fried as technical cofounder.
Co-founded FTX as chief technology officer and major shareholder.
FTX collapsed; he pleaded guilty and agreed to cooperate with prosecutors.
Testified in United States v. Bankman-Fried regarding FTX/Alameda code privileges and fraud.
Sentenced with cooperation credit; avoided prison time for his FTX role.

name: Shou Zi Chew
milestone_by_age_26: By age 26 (2009) he had finished UCL economics (2006), worked at Goldman Sachs in London, and was en route to a Harvard MBA (2010); partner role at DST Global, Xiaomi CFO, ByteDance CFO, and TikTok CEO all came at ages well above 26.
early_history_summary: Born Singapore 1 January 1983; Hwa Chong Institution; National Service; UCL BSc economics 2006; Goldman Sachs; Harvard MBA 2010 with Facebook internship; DST Global partner investing in Chinese tech; Xiaomi CFO from 2015; ByteDance CFO then TikTok CEO from 2021.
family_context_summary: Father reportedly worked in construction and mother in bookkeeping (Straits Times profile).
evidence_summary: Wikipedia and Straits Times timeline place Goldman/UCL before 26 and major operator roles (DST, Xiaomi, TikTok) after.

name: Aisha Bowe
category: Aerospace engineer, STEMBoard CEO, spaceflight participant
milestone_by_age_26: By 2009 at about age 23–24 she completed a University of Michigan aerospace BS (2008) and space systems engineering MS (2009) and joined NASA Ames in the AST Flight and Fluid Mechanics group working on air-traffic management algorithms.
early_history_summary: Born Ann Arbor 4 November 1985; working-class path via Washtenaw Community College after being steered toward cosmetology; father encouraged math and was himself studying electrical engineering. Michigan aerospace degrees; NASA Ames trajectory/controls work; later founded STEMBoard and LINGO; Blue Origin NS-31 crew in 2025.
family_context_summary: Working-class U.S. upbringing; high school counselor pushed cosmetology; father pursued electrical engineering and encouraged her math coursework at community college.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father’s concurrent electrical engineering studies provided adjacent STEM modeling and encouragement rather than a formal industry pipeline.
primary_early_advantage_tags: community college transfer, Michigan aerospace, NASA Ames, father EE encouragement, Zurbuchen mentorship
evidence_summary: Wikipedia, Forbes, and NASA-related profiles corroborate Michigan degrees (2008–09) and NASA Ames flight-dynamics work by ~age 24, with later NSBE/NASA awards (2012), STEMBoard Inc. 5000 recognition, and Blue Origin NS-31 (2025). Early constraint (tracking advice, working-class start) and Michigan/NASA pipeline are the clearest early-advantage themes.
starting_point: Born 1985 in Ann Arbor to a working-class family; redirected from cosmetology advice into community college math and then Michigan aerospace engineering.
current_position: CEO of STEMBoard and founder of LINGO; Blue Origin NS-31 spaceflight participant (2025); STEM education and aerospace public figure.

trajectory.event: Earned BS in aerospace engineering from the University of Michigan after transferring from community college.
Completed MS in space systems engineering and joined NASA Ames Flight Trajectory Dynamics / AST Flight and Fluid Mechanics work.
Received NSBE Outstanding Technical Contribution and NASA honor awards for technical and EEO contributions.
STEMBoard named to Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing private U.S. companies.
Founded LINGO STEM education kits; later raised multimillion-dollar funding.
Flew Blue Origin NS-31 as science payload operator and crossed the Kármán line.

name: Grady Booch
milestone_by_age_26: In 1981 at age 25–26 he became Chief Scientist of Rational Software (Rational Machines) from the company's founding by Paul Levy and Mike Devlin, beginning a multi-decade leadership role in software engineering tools and methods.
early_history_summary: Born Amarillo, Texas, 27 February 1955; early IBM 1130 access via a local salesman; USAFA BS 1977; UCSB MS EE 1979; Air Force project/instructor roles; Rational Chief Scientist from 1981; Booch method; UML with Jacobson and Rumbaugh; IBM Fellow after Rational acquisition.
primary_leverage_engine: Early software methods depth + product company platform
family_context_summary: Not richly documented in reviewed sources beyond Texas origin and Air Force Academy path.
primary_early_advantage_tags: USAFA, early computer access, Rational founding CS role, Ada/OO methods wave, Vandenberg systems work
evidence_summary: Wikipedia states Chief Scientist from Rational’s 1981 founding at age ~26; USAFA/UCSB credentials and early Air Force systems work precede that. Later Booch method, UML, IBM Fellow, and Lovelace/Computer Pioneer awards cement tier-2 software-engineering stature. Family background remains thinly sourced.
starting_point: Born 1955 in Amarillo, Texas; early personal computing exposure on an IBM 1130; educated at the U.S. Air Force Academy and UCSB.
current_position: Chief Scientist for Software Engineering at IBM Research (embodied cognition / software engineering research); co-creator of UML and longtime software architecture public intellectual.

trajectory.event: Earned BS from the U.S. Air Force Academy and began Air Force engineering work including Vandenberg ground support.
Completed MS in electrical engineering at UC Santa Barbara and later instructed at the Air Force Academy.
Became Chief Scientist of Rational Software from the company's founding.
Published Software Engineering with Ada, establishing early methods authorship.
Published major Object-Oriented Analysis and Design with Applications (Booch method) editions influencing industry practice.
Helped create UML with Ivar Jacobson and James Rumbaugh as the unified modeling standard era took hold.
Rational acquired by IBM; named IBM Fellow and continued as senior software engineering scientist.
